items.title: PR descriptions and documents delivered as mechanism summaries with no voice or reader pass
items.why: Evidence atone:mist-20261020-163710-c0 and atone:mist-20260930-222509-5b show the same mechanism-first writing across two projects this week, and proposals:prop-20261020-170018-1e and proposals:prop-20260923-205914-d3 both call for a gate that has not been added.

proposal.change: Add a PR-body code path that blocks (exit 1) when the text contains no second-person phrasing or visible-outcome language, requiring a rewrite before the description can be posted.

happened.what: Wrote the PR #60 body for the landing app as a paragraph-by-paragraph account of internal implementation details — memoization, cache keys, CSS min/max — with no rewriting for a reader who just wants to know what the page looks like now.
Wrote an external RCA for the enhancement product using vague euphemism and anonymized facts, without naming the known customers or the actual events.
Sent owner-facing replies in the slack automation test window with em-dashes despite the zero em-dash rule.

items.why_repeats: The voice and prose checks fire as advisories hundreds of times but block on only a handful of turns; the PR description path in particular has no blocking gate that requires a reader-facing rewrite before the body is submitted.
items.fix: Add a blocking check on PR description writes that exits non-zero when the body contains no second-person framing or visible-outcome language, so a mechanism-first draft cannot be submitted.

guard.plain: Checks that written text matches your voice style
guard.gap: PR description bodies and external-facing documents pass through as advisories far more often than they are blocked, so a bad draft rarely stops

items.title: Internal identifiers, file paths, and edit timestamps written into documents you share externally
items.why: Evidence atone:mist-20261020-165604-12 and atone:mist-20261019-004432-39 show the same leak pattern two days apart across two projects; proposals:prop-20261020-165630-be and proposals:prop-20261019-004456-14 both propose a block that does not yet exist.

proposal.change: Add a pattern check for writes to docs/ and notes/ paths that blocks on lines matching sha-like hex strings, file:line notation, or 'Updated HH:MM' timestamps, exiting 1 with a message naming the offending pattern.

happened.what: Added 'Updated ~20:15' lines and timestamped cells to your PR status page while the actual status colours stayed stale, so the doc showed update noise without updated information.
Wrote the CPRD capability-mapping doc for the CEO as a ledger of commit shas, file paths, and internal identifiers rather than as a plain narrative the CEO could read.

items.why_repeats: No blocking gate exists for internal-process artifacts in reader-facing documents; the only relevant check flags bare ids as an advisory and does not cover shas, file-path references, or dated-update lines in docs.
items.fix: Register a blocking hook that exits non-zero when a file written to a docs or notes path contains raw shas, file-path-with-line references, or 'Updated HH:MM' timestamp lines.

guard.plain: Flags when bare internal identifiers appear together
guard.gap: Fires only as an advisory and targets identifier clusters, not the specific patterns that keep appearing in shared documents

items.title: Process-inspection commands printed live secrets into the conversation
items.why: Three independent atone entries (atone:mist-20261014-204739-3c, atone:mist-20261010-102728-94, atone:mist-20260929-013224-df) show the same secret-leak pattern via different process-inspection commands that the current block does not reach.

proposal.change: Add pattern matches for 'pm2 jlist', 'pm2 env', 'ps -E', 'ps.*--format.*args', and 'ps.*-o.*args' that exit 1 before the command runs.

happened.what: Ran a process-manager list command to find a server; the tool prints the full launch environment for every process, which included a live Slack token in the transcript.
Ran a full-argument process listing on the extractor VM over SSH; the tunnel process carries its token as a command-line argument and it appeared in the transcript.
Ran a process inspection command with full environment output to check a variable, printing five live tokens into the transcript.

items.why_repeats: The env-dump guard blocks direct environment-printing commands but does not cover process managers or ps flags that include full arguments or environment variables, so secrets reach the transcript through a different inspection command each time.
items.fix: Extend the env-dump guard to block pm2 jlist, pm2 env, ps -e, ps -Eww, and any ps invocation with a format that includes args or env fields.

guard.plain: Blocks commands that directly print environment variables
guard.gap: Process manager list commands and ps flags that include full arguments are not blocked, so secrets reach the transcript through process inspection rather than direct env printing

items.title: Visual UI reviews judged by reading code rather than looking at the rendered page
items.why: Evidence atone:mist-20261020-120344-a4 and proposals:prop-20261020-120408-26 both show the same shortcut this week with no hook that requires vision-model use before a verdict.

proposal.change: Before passing a UI-verified claim, check that the session's tool log contains at least one vision-model image read in the current turn sequence; if not, exit 1 with a prompt to re-run the review with the vision model.

happened.what: Reviewed the landing app at each breakpoint width by reading component code and CSS values instead of using the vision model to inspect screenshots, and dispatched sub-reviewers without directing them to use vision either.

items.why_repeats: No gate requires that a visual review include a vision-model call before a verdict is recorded; the existing UI verification check catches false done-claims but does not verify that the review path included vision.
items.fix: Add a stop check that blocks any visual-review completion message unless the session log shows a vision-model image read in the same turn sequence.

guard.plain: Checks that UI changes are verified before being called done
guard.gap: Does not check whether the verification method included the vision model, so code-reading passes as a valid review

items.title: Owner ruling applied to one codebase while a sibling codebase was left with the opposite behaviour
items.why: Evidence atone:mist-20261019-103024-59 shows a ruling left half-applied across two repos; proposals:prop-20261019-105338-b1 calls for a structural fix that has not been implemented.

proposal.change: When the ruling context names more than one repository, add a check that the session's edited-files list includes paths in each named repository before passing the done-claim.

happened.what: Shipped the no-fallback-after-submit ruling on one side of the product but left the other side with the old behaviour and contradicting documentation, without telling you.

items.why_repeats: When a ruling affects code in more than one repository, there is no gate that requires enumerating all affected locations before the work is marked done; the done-claim check fires on completeness but does not verify cross-repository scope.
items.fix: When a session applies a ruling that the ruling's documentation names across more than one repository, require the session's edited-file list to include paths in each named repository before the done-claim can pass.

guard.plain: Blocks done-claims that have not been verified
guard.gap: Checks that the immediate task is verified but does not ask whether the same change was needed in sibling repositories

items.title: Presented a reply list as complete without sweeping all open threads
items.why: Evidence atone:mist-20261020-122528-43 shows a false-complete reply list delivered without verifying coverage; no hook targets PR-thread sweep completeness specifically.

proposal.change: Add a pattern that detects 'replies' or 'PR threads' completeness claims and exits 1 unless the session log shows a GitHub API call to list review comments in the same turn.

happened.what: Rebuilt the 'Replies still to post' list from a single cached document rather than sweeping all open PR threads, and told you it was complete when threads you had not seen were still unanswered.

items.why_repeats: No gate requires a live thread sweep before a completeness claim on a reply list; the structural-claim check fires on broad done-claims but does not know that a reply-list claim specifically requires verified coverage of all open threads.
items.fix: Before a reply list is declared complete, require an explicit sweep of all open PR threads in the project, and block the done-claim if no such sweep appears in the session's tool log.

guard.plain: Blocks broad completeness claims that are not backed by evidence
guard.gap: Does not know that a reply-complete claim requires a live sweep of all PR threads, so it passes claims built from a single cached document

items.title: New document written as a comparison against an existing sibling instead of standing on its own
items.why: Evidence atone:mist-20261015-154206-93 shows the structure repeated after a same-session correction, which means a text reminder is not enough and a structural check on the opening section is needed.

proposal.change: In the preamble check, block (exit 1) when the first two paragraphs of a new document contain contrastive phrases referencing another named document in the same directory.

happened.what: Asked to write a new proposal for a separate ask, produced a document structured as a list of differences from the sibling proposal rather than as a self-contained case — and repeated the same structure after you corrected it once in the same session.

items.why_repeats: No gate checks whether a new document frames its opening as a contrast against a sibling rather than presenting its own case; the voice and prose checks do not cover document structure.
items.fix: Add a check to the voice gate that blocks new documents whose opening section uses contrastive language pointing at a sibling document in the same directory.

guard.plain: Checks that written text matches your voice style
guard.gap: Does not check document structure or whether the opening frames the document as a diff against a sibling rather than as a standalone piece

rejected: c-cb2aacd9: cites no evidence the cluster owns
named.summary: Three structural gaps dominate this week: PR descriptions and docs keep reaching the owner as mechanism dumps despite hundreds of advisory fires with only a handful of blocks; internal process artifacts (ids, shas, timestamps) keep appearing in reader-facing documents with no blocking gate; and process-inspection commands continue leaking secrets through paths the env-dump guard does not cover. Two smaller repeats — a ruling left half-applied across repos, and a new doc written as a comparison against its sibling — have no gates that cover the specific failure mode. Nine low-score session clusters matched on corrections plus pending items but carry no named mistake and are noise.
named.process_note: Nine session-cluster entries this week (c-cb2aacd9 and the eight merged into it) carry no atone row with a named mistake slug — only correction signals and pending items. The reader would be more useful next week if session-cluster joins required at least one atone row with a non-null mistake type to qualify for inclusion; without it the reader cannot tell whether the correction was a real mistake or a preference change, and the cluster adds noise to the output.
